articles.title: Your Body's Biggest and Smallest
articles.dek: Which bone is the longest? Which one is the smallest? The answers may surprise you.
paras: Your body is full of records. Which part is the biggest? Which bone is the longest? And which one is the smallest? Let's find out. You may be surprised!

The biggest organ in your body is your skin. It covers your whole body and keeps out dirt and germs. In an adult, skin is about two square metres. That is about as big as a single bed. Skin also tells your brain when something is hot or cold.

The longest bone is the thigh bone. Its name is the femur. It is in the top part of your leg. It is about one quarter of your height. If you are 1.6 metres tall, your femur is about 40 centimetres long. It must carry your weight when you walk, run and jump.

Now look at the smallest bone. It is in your ear, and its name is the stapes. It is only about three millimetres long. That is smaller than a grain of rice. It is the smallest bone in your body, but it is very important. It helps you hear sounds.

What about the hardest part of your body? That is the enamel on your teeth. It is harder than your bones. But it is not as strong as a good habit. Brush your teeth twice a day, and do not eat too many sweets.

Which record is the most surprising for you? Many students say the stapes is the most amazing. It is so small, but it works hard all day. Our bodies are not all the same, but every part is important. Look after the whole body: sleep well, eat well and move every day.

articles.title: Talent Show Night
articles.dek: Three students get ready for the school talent show. What can they do?
paras: Our school talent show is on Friday. Every student can join. You do not need to be a star. Last week, many students put their names on the list. Here, three students tell us about their acts and how they get ready.

Lucas, 13: I can play the guitar, but I can't sing well. When I was seven, I couldn't even hold a guitar! My uncle taught me. Now I can play ten songs. On Friday, my friend Ben will sing and I will play. Ben can sing very well, so we are a good team.

Amina, 14: I can do magic tricks. I started when I was ten. At first I couldn't hide the coin, and everyone could see it! Now I practise every day. I can make a coin disappear in two seconds. But I can't tell you how I do it. It is a secret!

Daniel, 12: I can't sing, dance or play music. But I can make people laugh. Last year I couldn't talk in front of the class, because I was shy. Now I can tell funny stories for five minutes. My sister says I can be very silly. That is the point!

Mrs Evans, the teacher: Thank you, everyone. You can all be proud of yourselves. Nobody can win if they do not try. Please come to the hall at six o'clock on Friday. Your family and friends can come too. Everybody can bring a cake to share. It will be a fun night, and we can all enjoy the show together.

articles.title: Rules at the Library
articles.dek: What must you do at the library? What mustn't you do?
paras: Welcome to Maple Town Library! You can find books, magazines and computers here. We have some rules, so everyone can enjoy the library. Please read these notices.
NOTICE 1: Quiet, please! You must speak quietly in the reading room. You mustn't use your phone for calls. If you need to talk, please go to the café.
NOTICE 2: Borrowing books. You must have a library card to borrow books. Children under 12 don't have to pay for a card. Other people have to pay two euros a year.
NOTICE 3: Returning books. You have to return books after three weeks. If a book is late, you must pay ten cents a day. You don't have to come in. You can use the box outside the door.
NOTICE 4: Computers. You must be ten or older to use a computer alone. You have to sign your name at the desk. You mustn't visit games sites. You don't have to pay for the computers.

Message from Sara to her brother Tom: Hi Tom! I'm at the library. I have to finish my homework here, so I can't go to the park. You don't have to wait for me. I must return two books too. See you at six! Sara
NOTICE 5: Closing time. The library closes at six o'clock on weekdays. You must leave your table tidy. You don't have to clean it, but please put the chairs back. Thank you!
